# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-27 (Extended v185)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to autumn Year 7. Primary locations include Paris—Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs, Rue Blomet, Rue de Rivoli, Place Louis XV, Champs-Élysées, Esplanade, bridge of the Invalides, Hôtel des Princes, Hôtel Meurice, Rue Saint-Honoré, Passage Delorme, Place du Palais-Royal, Rue de Béthisy, Rue des Bourdonnais, Rue de la Poterie, Rue du Contrat-Social, Marché-aux-Poirées, Rue de Babylone, Rue du Chaume, Rue des Vieilles-Haudriettes, Royal Printing Establishment, Luxembourg Garden, Rue de Pontoise. English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Wilholt, Torton, Quenford, Pontoise, Stenenridge, Gulhaven. Barrière d'Enfer, Esplanade de l'Observatoire.

## Rumored Claims and Established Facts

**Rumored claims (unverified)**: **Yera Stenworth confided to Nerine Prydenridge fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately (autumn Year 7—NEW)**. Fenelle Lindmere and Marald confided/revealed Stenson family once owed blood debt to Stenenridge family. Ferald Stenworth confided to Zavus Prydenridge same blood debt claim. Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood (autumn Year 6). In letter Ismira Stenson burned after reading, Elra revealed deed to Kelmere pastures was forged.

**Established facts**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford; Kassa later went to Dungate. Taric Corrley quit Staveford, took lodgings in Dungate. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead, took lodgings in Salcombe; Fenelle Lindmere followed within month. Ismira Stenson quit Dungate, took lodgings in Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Matho Stenson went to Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Elra Corrford settled in Elmhaven. Havie Prydenridge promised Gadrek Prydenridge to pay old debt to Stenworth family. **Gadrek Prydenridge gave up being a miller and took work as a brewer (autumn Year 7—NEW)**. Kassa Stenson's husband gave solemn promise to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe. Fenelle Lindmere found work in Elmhaven, moved there (summer Year 7). Marald Corrford followed to Elmhaven within month (summer Year 7). Zavus Prydenridge apprenticed anew and became ferryman (summer Year 7).

**Solemn promises**: Elra Corrford gave Matho Stenson solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven. Pelia gave Fenelle solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Salcombe (summer Year 7).

**New births and marriages (Spring Year 7)**: Rinelle Corrley and Kadrek Brackick had son Movus Brackick (Wilholt). Nerine Prydenridge and Lurald Stenworth wed at Ostcombe, had son Istho Stenworth (Ostcombe). Wenelle Lindmere and Rovus Prydenridge had son Febin Prydenridge (Kelmere). Bremira Corrford and Zavus Prydenridge married at Dunstead. Ferald and Zalis Corrley wed at Dunstead (summer Year 7), lived there thereafter.

**Broken faith**: Rorald Lindmere broke faith with Kassa Stenson—promised work (carry sealed letter to Torton) never begun.

## Spring/Summer/Autumn Year 7 Observations

Residents walked long way to avoid muddy square. Road rutted and puddled after thaw. **Someone chalked crooked sun on forge wall** (repeated observations, present in autumn Year 7). Multiple residents hummed childhood tunes while scrubbing steps: Yera, Rinelle, Zavus, Kadan, Bremira, Rorald Lindmere. **Nerine hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step; Lurald Stenworth hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step (autumn Year 7—NEW)**. **Matho, Bremira, Thizek, and Pelia each counted coins twice, came up penny short**. **Matho Stenson fell asleep in chair before fire had caught**. **Thizek Stenenridge fell asleep in chair before fire had caught**. River remarks—multiple residents observed river up; others said it always was in spring: Taric/Kassa, Sebin/Rorald Lindmere, Elra/Fenelle Lindmere, Zavus/Bremira Corrford, Thizek/Isvie, Isvie/Thizek. Ismira asked if it would rain; Fenelle only shrugged. Ismira and Bremira argued with carter over oat prices; Ferald also argued with carter. Kadan and Rovus talked of weather, harvest, lame horse; Rovus and Kadan discussed salt price scandal. Bremira and Ferald discussed salt price scandal. Yewyn and Pelia discussed salt price scandal. Fenelle said "The price of salt is a scandal"; Ismira agreed. Yera, Sebin, Pelia, Bremira, Thizek laughed at stories nobody else found funny. Yera and Zavus complained of aching backs. Pelia complained of aching back as usual. Luvie complained of aching back, as usual (Ostcombe). Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage. Gulls quarreled over fish heads by steps. Children chased hoop down lane. Cart loaded with turnips creaked past well. Yewyn, Tatho, Isvie Stenworth bought ribbon at stall and regretted it. Yewyn appeared tired; Pelia noted this. Tatho mended torn sleeve by window and said little. Bremira, Zavus, Fenelle Lindmere, Thizek Stenenridge mended torn sleeve by window and said little. **Yera Stenworth mended torn sleeve by window and said little (autumn Year 7—NEW)**. "Will it rain?" asked Tatho; Rorald shrugged. **"Will it rain, do you think?" asked Vesmira; Isric Thornmere only shrugged (autumn Year 7, Ostcombe—NEW)**. **"You look tired," Ilrald told Isric Thornmere, who did not deny it (autumn Year 7, Ostcombe—NEW)**. **"You look tired," Vesmira told Movie Prydenridge, who did not deny it (barricade period—NEW)**. Tatho spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight. **Istho Stenworth spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight (autumn Year 7—NEW)**. Baker's boy late again, line at oven grew long (repeated). **Lurald Stenworth read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints (autumn Year 7—NEW)**. Zavus and Fenelle read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints. **Frost had silvered hedges overnight**. **Wind came off water with smell of salt and tar**. Rain threatened since morning but held off. **Nerine watched clouds and predicted rain, wrongly (autumn Year 7, Ostcombe—NEW)**. **Movie Prydenridge walked long way round to avoid muddy square (autumn Year 7, Ostcombe—NEW)**.

## Jean Valjean's Crisis and Discovery

**Blotting-book discovery (night 24th June 1832)**: Upon arriving at Rue de l'Homme Armé lodgings, Valjean found Cosette's blotting-book revealing letter to young workman in Rue Plumet. Valjean understood Cosette was escaping; another was goal of her heart. Soul gave utter roar. Into paternity his life's widowhood introduced all shades of love—daughter, mother, sister, woman, wife. Grief surpassed bounds; quiver of revolt ran head to foot; immense reawakening of egotism; the *I* howled. **Rue de l'Homme Armé lodgings**: Two sleeping-rooms, dining-room, kitchen, garret for Toussaint on second floor, back court. **Valjean at barricade (6th June, dawn)**: Took aim at fireman acting as sentinel on neighboring roof, smashed his helmet with bullet. When officer replaced sentinel, Valjean took aim again, sent officer's casque away. Officer retired speedily. No further attempts to spy on barricade made thereafter. Stared silently at wall opposite during barricade phase.

## Marius and Cosette's Romance

**Recognition and love**: Cosette acknowledged she never forgot Marius, always loved him. Beginning autumn Year 5, Marius came every evening. **Confessions (spring Year 6)**: Marius told Cosette—orphan, name Marius Pontmercy, lawyer, father colonel and hero. Cosette told Marius—brought up at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent. **Éponine's death (evening 24th June)**: Éponine revealed she led Marius to barricade, spoke of her death as blessing. Gave Marius letter from Cosette before dying. **Cosette's letter content**: Marriage impossible; grandfather refuses; no fortune; hastened to him, he gone; kept promise given; dies; loves him. **Marius joins barricade (evening 24th June)**: Upon learning Valjean plans England departure in one week, arranged meeting 26th June. Same evening, rushed to barricade of Rue de la Chanvrerie. **During first phase**: Witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed; flung self into conflict. Saved Gavroche with first shot. **Mental state (6th June, dawn)**: Fasting, fevered, emerged from all hope, plunged into visionary stupor. Felt he had entered tomb. **Marius recognizes Inspector (6th June)**: Upon seeing inspector of Rue de Pontoise striding over barricade to his death, Marius recalled inspector had handed him two pistols, which he used in this barricade. Recalled inspector's face and name.

**Cosette's current state (summer Year 7, morning)**: Slept soundly, awoke with sun. First thought smiling; felt thoroughly reassured. Three days since saw Marius. Certain he would come. Back court surrounded by high walls. Burst into tears. Observed martin's nest in ancient cornice. Watched mother spread wings like fan over brood; father fluttered about bearing food. Cosette, hair in sunlight, soul absorbed in chimæras, bent over and began gazing at birds with profound trouble virgin nest produces.

## Barricade of Rue de la Chanvrerie (24th June into 6th June)

**Café Corinthe**: Ground floor with bar; first floor with billiard-table and spiral staircase; cellar via trap-door; lodgings and attics. Proprietor: Widow Hucheloup. Serving-maids: Matelote, Gibelotte. **Two barricades**: Larger shut off Rue de la Chanvrerie; other closed Rue Mondétour. **Larger barricade (6th June, dawn)**: Height six or seven feet, stepped construction, paling-stones, casks, wheels, omnibus pole with ropes, red flag. Forty-three insurgents. **Three-front fortification**: Walled on Rue de la Chanvrerie (front), Rues du Cygne and de la Petite Truanderie (left), Rue Mondétour (right). Almost impregnable but fatally hemmed in. No exit.

**Enjolras's orders (6th June)**: Directed two-thirds of piled stones from Corinthe door carried to first floor and attic. Within two minutes, stones walled up sash-window on first floor and roof windows to half height. Loop-holes carefully planned by Feuilly, principal architect, allowed gun-barrel passage. Ordered eight guns kept loaded, swords and pistols in belts. Twenty men to barricade. Six ambushed in attic windows and first-floor window to fire through loop-holes. Upon drum beating assault, twenty below stairs to rush barricade.

**Tactical observations**: Defenders sparing of ammunition; assailants know this, combine arrangements with irritating leisure, expose themselves prematurely though in appearance more than reality. Preparations for attack made with methodical deliberation; thereafter, lightning strikes. Two cannons discharged ball against centre of barrier to make breach for assault.

**Javert's arrest**: Identified as Inspector of Police, aged fifty-two. Bound with whip-cord about feet. Remarked upon seeing Valjean: "It is perfectly simple."

**Le Cabuc execution**: Enjolras executed him for killing, justified by insurrection needing discipline.

**M. Mabeuf's sacrifice**: Venerable, austere, aged eighty. Evening 24th June: tore flag from Enjolras, upholding red banner with aged arm. Enjolras eulogized: magnificent death; presence renders barricade impregnable. Body lay in kitchen on table.

**Gavroche's role (6th June)**: Young gamin, fearless, collected cartridges under heavy fire. Called invulnerable dwarf of the fray. One better-aimed bullet finally struck him; Gavroche staggered and sank. Whole barricade cried out. He remained in sitting posture, raised both arms, began to sing. **Éponine's corpse**: Discovered after crossing barrier. Livid face, streaming hair, pierced hand, half-nude breast. Corner of houses hid them from insurgents. Corpses from barricade formed terrible pile nearby.

**Two lost children in Luxembourg Garden (6th June, daytime)**: One aged seven, one aged five, pale and ragged. Smaller said "I am very hungry." Elder broke brioche into two portions, took small one for himself, gave large one to brother. Swans on water; child used stick to retrieve cake before swans reached it.

**Broader situation (6th June morning)**: Musketry and grape-shot alternated. Barricades begun in Rue du Poirier and Rue des Gravilliers. Woman fired on National Guard from behind blind in Rue Saint-Denis. Child aged fourteen arrested with pockets full of cartridges. Four cannons echoed mournfully. Columns attempted to scale redoubt. Two-thirds of gunners lying beneath wheels. Smoke created twilight in daylight. Everything contributed to tragic majesty: mysterious crashes, armed masses in streets, intermittent cavalry gallop, artillery shock, squad firing, cannonades crossing in Paris labyrinth, battle smoke mounting gilded above roofs, indescribable cries, menace lightnings everywhere, tocsin of Saint-Merry with accents of sob, mildness of weather, sky splendor filled with sun and clouds, beauty of day, alarming silence of houses.

**Broader principles on insurrection**: When hour came and people wished to end prolonged situation, city consented to paving-stone tearing; inhabitant became combatant's auxiliary; house fraternized with fortress. When situation not ripe, masses disowned movement, city turned desert, souls grew chilled, refuges nailed up, street became defile for army. Utopia impatient becomes revolt, knows catastrophe awaits, comes too soon, becomes resigned, accepts catastrophe, serves those denying it without complaint. Indomitable facing obstacles, gentle towards ingratitude. Utopia borrows battle mode from yesterday's lie, becomes deed of violence, shoots spies, executes traitors, suppresses living beings, flings them into darkness. Uses death. No sword simple; every blade has two edges; he who wounds with one is wounded with other.

**Progress philosophical observations**: Progress is man's mode of existence, general life of human race. Advances toward celestial and divine. Has halting-places, stations, nights of sleep. Despair is wrong. Progress infallibly awakes, marches on even asleep. When erect again, found taller. Individual has distinct interests, can stipulate for them without forfeiture. Present has pardonable egotism. Momentary life has rights, not bound to sacrifice constantly to future. Generations equal, have their turns. Until universal peace and harmony established, progress will have revolutions as halting-places.
